Another interesting tidbit from the 80s, I don't think that VCR games ever really took off as they're a really clunky and cumbersome concept and most of the time the low-quality of the video just detracts away from what might have been a decent board game.

The only one of these I ever had was Party Mania (1993) and I can't remember being aware that there were ever any others made until years after VHS had become obsolete.

Basically VCR games were traditional board games that had video elements awkwardly shoehorned into them, such as Candyland and Clue and even charades, somehow.

Naturally there were also tons of games made based on popular TV shows and films like Star Trek and Wayne's World.

Typically the gameplay involved just playing a normal board game but with a video that either ran continually or that had to be paused and started when you were prompted by cards and that featured horrible actors trying to interact with you in a really ham-handed and unintentionally hilarious way.

The acting is terrible across the board, even in cases like the Wayne's World game that featured the real Mike Myers and Dana Carvey. That one is the worst to watch, in my opinion, because it's impossible to watch them slogging through this embarrassing mess and not wonder what was going through their minds as they filmed this.

I'll link some clips to some of the games below and I highly recommend watching a a couple minutes of the Wayne's World one, the Star Trek one and Party Mania. They're the three with the worst acting, most embarrassing dialogue and are the most dated and cringe-inducing.
